userStories.title: Technical SEO foundation: sitemap.xml, robots.txt, and meta tag audit on existing pages
userStories.description: As a developer, I want a sitemap.xml, robots.txt, and complete meta tags on all 5 existing pages so search engines can properly discover and index the site.
acceptanceCriteria: Create landing/sitemap.xml with entries for all 5 existing pages (index.html, features.html, privacy.html, terms.html, invite.html) using https://bookisports.com/ as base URL
Each sitemap entry has <loc>, <lastmod> (2026-02-24), and <changefreq> (weekly for index/features, monthly for privacy/terms/invite)
Create landing/robots.txt with User-agent: *, Allow: /, Sitemap: https://bookisports.com/sitemap.xml
Audit privacy.html: add missing OG tags (og:type, og:url, og:title, og:description, og:image) and Twitter card tags matching the pattern in index.html
Audit terms.html: add missing OG tags and Twitter card tags
Audit invite.html: add missing OG tags and Twitter card tags
Add <link rel='canonical' href='https://bookisports.com/[page]'> to ALL 5 pages (index.html, features.html, privacy.html, terms.html, invite.html)
Verify features.html already has OG/Twitter tags — add any missing ones
All meta descriptions are unique per page and under 160 characters
HTML validates and page renders correctly
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill
userStories.notes: This is the foundation story — no new pages, just improving existing ones. The index.html and features.html already have OG+Twitter tags (see their <head> sections). The privacy.html and terms.html are missing OG/Twitter tags entirely. Use the same og:image (https://bookisports.com/assets/og-image.png) across all pages. Canonical URLs should NOT include .html extension if the site uses clean URLs, but since this is static HTML on Netlify, use the actual file paths (e.g., https://bookisports.com/features.html). Check landing/netlify.toml for any URL rewriting rules that might affect canonical URLs.

userStories.title: Schema markup: Organization, FAQ, and Article structured data
userStories.description: As a developer, I want schema.org structured data on key pages so search engines can display rich results.
acceptanceCriteria: Add Organization schema (JSON-LD) to index.html: name, url, logo, description, sameAs (social links if any)
Add WebSite schema to index.html with name, url, and potentialAction (SearchAction)
Add FAQ schema (JSON-LD) to pph-software-alternative.html with 3-4 relevant Q&A pairs
Add FAQ schema to how-to-run-your-own-sportsbook.html with 3-4 relevant Q&A pairs
Add FAQ schema to bookie-ledger-software.html with 3-4 relevant Q&A pairs
Add Article schema (JSON-LD) to all 4 blog posts: headline, author, datePublished, dateModified, description, image, publisher
All JSON-LD blocks are in <script type='application/ld+json'> tags in the <head>
JSON is valid (no trailing commas, proper escaping)
HTML validates and page renders correctly
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill
userStories.notes: JSON-LD is the preferred format for schema.org markup. Place all structured data in the <head> of each page. Organization schema on index.html: { '@context': 'https://schema.org', '@type': 'Organization', 'name': 'Booki', 'url': 'https://bookisports.com', 'logo': 'https://bookisports.com/assets/logo-booki-blk.svg', 'description': 'Modern pick management software for independent organizers.' }. For FAQ schema, write natural Q&A pairs that match what users might search — e.g., 'What is PPH software?', 'How do I track weekly settlements?'. For Article schema, use author: { '@type': 'Organization', 'name': 'Booki' }, publisher same. datePublished: '2026-02-24'.
